--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): ok everyone hi thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, sounds like we have the slatepoint squad, thanks for making time
[00:08] Priya (SlatePoint): hi thanks, priya here, we have about 20 minutes of questions then want to see the sandbox run, ideally focus on reliability and cost
[00:15] Maya (Redwood): great, we'll do a short context ask then jump into a live sandbox, carlos will drive the demo. quick prov: are you running the summarization in a streaming low-latency path or batch offline?
[00:25] Ethan (SlatePoint): streaming — when alerts fire we want a summary fast, like <500ms ideally for single-turn short summaries, longer for bigger docs. also cost matters, we will be token heavy so minimizing unit cost is key
[00:38] Carlos (Redwood): got it. for streaming use cases we show two patterns: incremental streaming for UX and short latency SLOs, or pre-batched requests with KV prefix caching if you have repeated context. i'll demo both.
[00:50] Samir (SlatePoint): quick Q — do you have any built in dedupe or stateful reassembly for partial tokens if connection drops?
[00:58] Carlos (Redwood): good question. we do not mutate client state — we stream partial tokens and expose offsets. typical pattern: client buffers the last N tokens and on reconnect uses request id to resume, or we implement idempotent request ids so you can safely retry without duplicate charges. i'll show the headers and sample code.
[01:15] Jules (Redwood): also, our SDK supports resumable streams that reattach to the same generation id when possible, otherwise we fall back to a quick reconciliation. note there are some edge transcriptions here where id names get funky (the auto transcription will sometimes show Redwood Dediked etc)
[01:30] Priya (SlatePoint): ha yeah we've seen weird names, fine. show the sandbox please.
[01:33] Carlos (Redwood): switching to screen, i'll run a live request from our node sandbox. first request: temp 0.2, max_tokens 150, streaming true. watch the partial chunks arrive.
[01:48] [console logs] Carlos (Redwood): "\> POST /v1/generate
  body: {prompt: 'summarize alert', temperature: 0.2, max_tokens:150, stream:true}
[02:05] [stream chunk] Speaker 2: 'Alert: CPU high on node-3...'
[02:10] Ethan (SlatePoint): ok we see partials coming in, that's good. is there a recommended chunk size or flush frequency?
[02:18] Carlos (Redwood): generally we flush on sentence or punctuation boundaries. the runtime batches based on a time window + token thresholds. you can tune client-side latency by adjusting the stream buffer or server 'flush_interval' metadata if needed.
[02:34] Maya (Redwood): also note the console shows token cost estimate in realtime per request so you can correlate latency with token usage.
[02:40] Priya (SlatePoint): about retries: if a stream fails mid-response, do we re-request and get charged twice for the same content?
[02:47] Carlos (Redwood): good one. there are two patterns: 1) optimistic retry with idempotency keys — you pass a user-provided request_id and we dedupe on the server for a short window, 2) client-side resume using the last event id to request continuation. dedupe is not indefinite, it's a bounded window to prevent unbounded state.
[03:04] Laura (SlatePoint): and what about backoff recommendations for heavy spikes? we have bursts when an incident causes many alerts at once.
[03:12] Carlos (Redwood): recommended: exponential backoff with jitter, and a graceful degradation path: route to a cheaper fallback model (we showed that in the docs) or return a short template-based summary. Optimize can recommend batching and cache heuristics to reduce peak QPS.
[03:28] Samir (SlatePoint): are fallbacks automatic? or we need to manage them?
[03:32] Jules (Redwood): you can configure routing policies — automatic fallback to a compat model or region wise. for POC we usually set up a canary: if latency spikes or token cost threshold hits, route subsequent requests to a smaller model variant.
[03:45] Priya (SlatePoint): ok, security checklist — SAML SSO, SOC2, keys, audit logs, data at rest encryption? we need all of those for procurement speed.
[03:55] Maya (Redwood): yep, we have SOC 2 Type II, SAML/SSO integrations, granular RBAC, KMS for customer-managed key options, and audit logs per account. i'll attach the security pack after the call.
[04:06] Priya (SlatePoint): KMS — does that apply to embeddings/kv cache as well?
[04:11] Jules (Redwood): yes, and for private deployments we support customer HSM/KMS. hosted has an option to integrate with your cloud KMS via key-wrapping.
[04:21] [06:00] Carlos (Redwood): jumping back to param discussion — temperature and top_p tradeoffs. lower temp gives more deterministic summaries; for alerting we'd recommend temp 0.0-0.3. max_tokens correlates directly with cost; also consider truncation vs instructing model to compress.
[06:35] Ethan (SlatePoint): our pipeline sometimes uses a 3k token context, will that blow cost?
[06:42] Carlos (Redwood): costs scale with context length; we suggest aggressive context trimming and using prefix KV cache when you have stable historical context. Optimize can analyze your prompt set and recommend quantization and batching to lower cost.
[06:58] Priya (SlatePoint): any hard limits we should plan for on hosted? e.g., per-second token caps?
[07:05] Maya (Redwood): hosted has tiered QPS and token rate limits per account; Dedicated gives predictable throughput and reserved capacity. for an SLO like 500ms we'd typically recommend a dedicated pool for consistent latency at scale, but many customers start hosted and migrate when usage stabilizes.
[07:24] Samir (SlatePoint): can you demo a retry scenario? maybe simulate a mid-stream disconnect and resume?
[07:30] Carlos (Redwood): yep, i'll simulate a dropped socket. watch the client reconnect and request resume with request_id X.
[07:40] [console] Carlos (Redwood): disconnecting... reconnecting with header: {"x-request-id":"slatepoint-12345", "x-resume-offset": 92}
[07:55] [stream] Speaker 1 (partial): '...continued summary: the incident impacted two services...'
[08:02] Ethan (SlatePoint): nice — and charging?
[08:06] Carlos (Redwood): if dedupe window contains original request we avoid double-charge for already-completed tokens; if not, we charge resumed tokens only. we'll include a sample billing trace so you can see token events per request.
[08:20] Priya (SlatePoint): about concurrency — we may have many clients hitting at same time, do you recommend client-side pooling or server pooling?
[08:29] Jules (Redwood): client-side multiplexing is often best — maintain a small pool of persistent connections to reduce TLS/handshake overhead. server side we handle multiplexing and batching automatically.
[08:40] Maya (Redwood): i'm going to open the console briefly to show the request insights and Optimize suggestions.
[08:45] [screen share] Maya (Redwood): console shows per-route latency, token breakdown, tail latency percentiles and per-model recommendations: quantize to int8 for this workload, enable prefix cache for repeated contexts, and set a default temp of 0.2 for alerts.
[09:10] Laura (SlatePoint): can Optimize do automated suggestions on live traffic or is it manual?
[09:15] Jules (Redwood): it ingests anonymized usage to make suggestions; you can also run offline evals with your prompt set. suggestions include batch sizes, quantization, and model splits for lower tail latency.
[09:30] Samir (SlatePoint): procurement will ask about data residency — can we pin region?
[09:34] Maya (Redwood): yes, you can pin to region and we have Private options for VPC or on-prem where all control plane components live in your network.
[09:40] Priya (SlatePoint): ok good. one last thing — how do we run a POC? timeline?
[09:45] Maya (Redwood): typical POC: 2 weeks. week one is integration and smoke tests, week two is load and quality checks. we'll provide a quickstart repo, a load script, and basic SLAs for the POC.
[09:55] [11:12] Carlos (Redwood): showing sample code snippet for retry/backoff: exponential backoff + jitter, idempotency key header example; also show the small helper that computes resume offset based on event stream. note: transcriptions sometimes show 'K-V cash' instead of KV cache in the auto text, so ignore that.
[11:40] Ethan (SlatePoint): on cost — can you share a calculator for projected monthly spend given our QPS?
[11:45] Maya (Redwood): yes, we'll send a token calculator. it's based on request tokens + prompt tokens + response tokens and includes caching effects.
[11:52] Priya (SlatePoint): are there compliance docs for SOC2 and encryption that we can share with procurement?
[11:58] Maya (Redwood): yes, will attach SOC 2 Type II report, encryption whitepaper, and our SAML integration guide.
[12:05] Samir (SlatePoint): any gotchas migrating from hosted to dedicated?
[12:10] Jules (Redwood): mainly network and capacity planning; dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and consistent throughput but requires slightly more setup time. we can help with the migration plan during the POC.
[12:22] Ethan (SlatePoint): minor note: we use internal feature flags to switch models, can Redwood expose route-level config in API?
[12:29] Carlos (Redwood): yes per-route configs are supported via the console and API; you can pin model versions and rollout with canaries.
